title: Glass Hook v12 (bass climb into A')
comment:
# Glass Hook

A clean guitar hook with designed bends in E minor at 90 BPM in 4/4, over a half-time trap groove. It runs 28 bars and loops whole, with the last bar dovetailing into the intro.

## Form

| Section | Bars | Chords | What happens |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Intro | 1–4 | Cmaj7–D6–Em9–Bm7 | Rhodes arpeggios alone over 8th hats and rim, a snare build into A |
| A | 5–12 | Cmaj7–D6–Em9–Bm7, twice | The hook over the trap groove and sub bass, Rhodes stabs, vibraphone above |
| B | 13–20 | Am9–Bm7–Cmaj7–D6, Am9–Bm7–Cmaj7–B7 | Calmer 8th-paced melody, Rhodes 3+3+2 phrase then half notes, guitar 2 a third below on the second pass, bass climb on B7 |
| A' | 21–28 | Cmaj7–D6–Em9–Bm7, twice | Crash, guitar 2 doubles the arpeggio bars and harmonizes the runs a third below |

## Tracks

| Track | Part |
| --- | --- |
| Lead guitar | The hook and the B melody |
| Guitar 2 | Harmony in B, double and harmony in A' |
| Rhodes | Intro arpeggios, stabs, B's broken chords |
| Vibraphone | Two high chord tones per bar above the guitar in A and A' |
| Pad | Quiet bed |
| Sub bass | Roots, the B7 climb into A' |
| Drums | Trap groove, thinner hats and shaker in B, tom fill |

## Guitar

- The hook is written from the fretboard: odd bars are a string-skipping arpeggio rising to D5 bent a whole step to E5, even bars are sextuplet runs, and the fourth bar's peak bends E5 to F#5.
- B reuses both bends and adds A4 bent to B4, and its B7 bar ends E5 bent to F#5, pulled off to D#5, leading back into the hook.
- Guitar 2 is a separately played take a few milliseconds late, panned opposite the lead, and stays under it as an inner voice.
- On B7 the sub bass climbs B1 D#2 F#2 A2, and A' lands on Cmaj7 as a deceptive resolution.
- In the last bar of A' the band falls away and the Rhodes starts the intro arpeggio, so the loop keeps running.
